summary: Cozumel is classic Caribbean drift diving with short boat rides, warm water, and consistently clear conditions. The island runs on a reliable two-tank morning rhythm with optional afternoon and night dives for anyone who wants to stack time underwater.
narrative: Cozumel delivers effortless walls and reef drifts with easy logistics, which makes it ideal for both first-time tropical travelers and repeat trips. Expect gentle current management, steady boat schedules, and an experience that feels dialed-in from gear setup to surface intervals. It is a place where you can dive hard without burning time on complicated transfers.

resort.description: Iberostar Waves Cozumel pairs a beachfront all-inclusive setup with an on-site dive center, making it easy to rinse, store, and re-kit between dives. The on-property operation keeps the pace smooth, with minimal transportation time and straightforward daily schedules.

dayToDay: Most days run a two-tank morning with optional afternoon or night dives. Boats leave early, return for lunch, and give plenty of surface time to reset. Drift profiles are planned around current, so groups stay together and surface with an SMB when needed.
resortDetails: On-site dive ops simplify the routine: gear lockers, rinse areas, and short walks to the dock. The resort layout keeps meals and downtime close, so you can dive hard without burning energy on logistics.
seasonality: Year-round destination with best visibility in winter and spring. Summer brings warmer water and calmer seas, while late summer can introduce brief storms without shutting down the entire season.
logistics: Fly into CUN and ferry to Cozumel, or take direct flights into CZM when available. Plan for airport transfers and ferry timing, and carry small bills for port fees and tips.
logisticsDetails: Plan a buffer day if you route through Cancun, since ferry timing can shift with weather. Marine park fees are typically collected daily. Bring a lightweight jacket for breezy boat rides and reef-safe sunscreen.

summary: Lake Michigan is a wreck-diver playground with crisp structure preserved by cold water. Expect deeper profiles, layered thermoclines, and dives that feel like a living history tour.
narrative: The Great Lakes deliver some of the best freshwater wreck diving in the country, with intact wood and steel resting in cold, dark water. A typical day starts early with detailed briefings, a short run to the site, and methodical dives that reward precise planning. It is a big-water trip that feels technical without being overly complex when planned well.

resort.description: Shipwreck Explorers runs small-group charters with site selection based on conditions and diver experience. The focus is on safe briefings, conservative profiles, and well-organized boat operations.

dayToDay: Expect early departures, a single long ride or two shorter runs, and two structured dives. Surface intervals are spent warming up and reviewing dive plans, with careful attention to ascent rates and deco limits.
resortDetails: Small-charter operations keep groups tight and flexible. Bring layers, dry storage, and plan for limited onboard space compared to tropical boats.
seasonality: Late spring through early fall; peak conditions are July to September. Early season dives are colder but can offer excellent visibility and fewer crowds.
logistics: Drive or fly into Milwaukee or Chicago and plan 1-3 hours to port towns. Weather windows matter, so build in buffer time if possible.
logisticsDetails: Charters are heavily weather-dependent, and cold fronts can shift plans quickly. Pack extra gloves, hats, and towels for surface intervals, and expect colder thermoclines below.

summary: Key Largo is the easiest way to pack warm-water dives into a short trip, with shallow reefs and accessible wrecks. Short boat rides and predictable conditions make it a high-value, low-stress destination.
narrative: Key Largo runs on simple logistics: drive or fly in, board a boat, and dive. Mornings often focus on reefs with optional wrecks or deeper sites later in the day. It is a reliable option for new divers, family trips, or anyone who wants a straightforward warm-water schedule without leaving the country.

resort.description: Sea Dwellers Dive Center provides consistent daily departures and easy access to both reefs and wrecks. The operation keeps the pace efficient, with short rides and clear briefings.

dayToDay: Most operators run two-tank morning dives with optional afternoon or night trips. Reefs are often first, with wrecks later in the day depending on conditions.
resortDetails: Local dive shops are set up for quick check-in, gear storage, and easy boarding. The town offers plenty of lodging options, from budget motels to resorts.
seasonality: Year-round; summer offers the warmest water and calmer seas. Winter can be breezier with occasional surface chop.
logistics: Fly into MIA or FLL and drive 1.5-2 hours to Key Largo. Domestic travel keeps things simple with no passport required.
logisticsDetails: Plan for traffic on the Overseas Highway, especially on weekends. Most boats depart from central marinas with easy parking and check-in.

narrative: Haigh is built for training: stable entry points, known depths, and predictable conditions. Day-to-day diving is simple, with short surface walks and lots of room to run drills or practice buoyancy. It is a low-effort way to stay current without a big travel plan.

summary: Playa del Carmen blends reef dives with cenote day trips for a varied itinerary. It is a compact travel plan with strong logistics and big highlights.
narrative: Playa is a two-for-one destination: warm-water reefs offshore and dramatic caverns inland. A typical week mixes boat dives with full-day cenote excursions and seasonal bull shark trips. It is a high-impact trip without long transfers, and it suits divers who want variety more than pure repetition.

resort.description: Dressel Divers Playa supports reef and cenote operations with coordinated transport and clear briefings. The shop makes it easy to build a flexible week around conditions and group preferences.

dayToDay: Reef days are boat-based with two-tank trips, while cenote days start earlier with transport inland and two dives per cenote. Expect longer surface intervals on cenote days and slightly cooler water.
resortDetails: Dive shops coordinate transport and timing for cenotes, which removes most of the planning burden. Lodging and dining are plentiful within walking distance.
seasonality: Cenotes run year-round, while bull sharks are strongest November through February. Summer brings warmer water and calm seas.
logistics: Fly into CUN and plan 45-60 minutes to Playa del Carmen. Cenote days require earlier starts and longer transport times inland.
logisticsDetails: Cenote entrance fees and transport are often paid in cash. Bring extra layers for air-conditioned transport and cooler freshwater dives.

summary: Warm reef and wall dives with short rides and a relaxed daily pace. Easy Caribbean logistics without feeling rushed.
narrative: Roatan keeps the plan simple: quick transfers, short boat rides, and plenty of surface time between dives. The walls add drama, the reefs stay colorful, and the rhythm works for mixed-experience groups. Tell us your dates and cert level, and we will build the right schedule.

resort.description: Tranquil Seas Roatan is a quiet, boutique eco-lodge with a small-room feel, tropical garden setting, and Caribbean Sea views. The on-site Sunken Fish restaurant, yoga classes, and dive center keep the schedule simple and stress-free.

dayToDay: Most days include two or three boat dives with relaxed surface intervals back at the resort or on the boat. Night dives are easy to add when conditions are calm, and the on-site dive center keeps gearing up simple.
resortDetails: Tranquil Seas keeps groups small and the pace relaxed. The tropical garden setting, sea views, and on-site restaurant make it easy to recharge between dives, while yoga and quiet spaces add a calm, resort-first feel.
seasonality: Year-round; spring and summer are calm with warm water. Late summer can bring brief storms but diving remains strong.
logistics: Fly into RTB; 20-45 minute transfer depending on lodging. Seasonal direct flights make travel easier at peak times.
logisticsDetails: US dollars are widely accepted. Transfers are short, but plan extra time for airport congestion on busy travel days. Tranquil Seas sits in Sandy Bay (Cahoon Bight), about 8 miles from RTB.

summary: Southern California delivers kelp forests, sea lions, and dramatic light in cooler Pacific water. Shore diving keeps costs down and allows flexible timing.
narrative: Catalina and the SoCal coastline feel like a different planet compared to tropical reefs. Giant kelp, surge channels, and playful wildlife create a dynamic dive that rewards solid buoyancy. A typical day is built around shore entries or short boat rides, with plenty of time to explore topside between dives.

resort.description: Casino Point is a classic shore-dive hub with easy access, clear entry points, and a wide range of depth profiles. It supports everything from beginner checkouts to deeper excursions.

summary: The Similan Islands deliver liveaboard-style diving with remote sites and big topography. Expect multiple dives per day and a focused dive schedule.
narrative: Thailand liveaboards run a dive, eat, sleep, repeat rhythm with four dives a day and access to sites day boats cannot reach. The Similans are known for granite boulders, vibrant reefs, and occasional pelagics. It is a high-value trip for divers who want volume, variety, and a true expedition feel.

resort.description: A dedicated liveaboard setup keeps you close to the best sites and maximizes bottom time. The experience is structured, with fixed schedules and planned meals between dives.

resortDetails: Liveaboard cabins are compact but functional, with dedicated gear stations and rinse areas. The crew manages schedules tightly to maximize diving time.
seasonality: Best November to April; parks often close May to October. Peak season offers the calmest seas and best visibility.
logistics: Fly into HKT and transfer to Khao Lak pier. Liveaboards have fixed departure times, so build in arrival buffers.
logisticsDetails: National park fees and fuel surcharges are common. Pack light but include multiple swimwear options and reef protection.
